about: Key-history bundle vectors (op:identity history, whisper identity verify). Each case is the bundle pages exactly as served, the _whisper-kel head they are checked against as TXT character-strings in hex (null: a DNSSEC-proven absence), the verifier's own clock, head-seen time and lag window, whether the log key below is used to verify each checkpoint, and the outcome. The subject is the identity the caller asked about, from its own knowledge (never the bundle's fields). Failure, verdict and proof names are stable. Every refusal must be refused by a bundle reader; reason_contains is the Java reader's wording, a hint, not a contract. A bundle reader is liberal in layout and ignores unknown fields; the server writes one canonical form (keys in code-point order, no whitespace between tokens, plain decimal integers, strings escaping quote and backslash with a backslash, newline as backslash-n, any other character outside U+0020..U+007E as backslash-u and four lowercase hex digits).
